[b]Story: 7/10[/b]
Very anime-esq but bunch of plot twits. They introduce some cool themes in the beginning but overtime they are forgotten or overshadowed due to the scope of the mainstory line (minor spoiler but government surveillance, media and such).  IMO the dual story didn't cause any dissonance confusion for the core storyline. I would say on the second playthrough with the next main character,  it answers and explains things pretty well. The main issue is due to the hangout feature. Its a strange hanging out at your hideout or a hangout episode with funky music in the background and everyone having fun despite something tragic happening, Maybe i'm a weeb but i found the story cool and wasn't difficult to follow (even with 2 storylines going at once).

[b]Music: 10/10 (or 5/10 if you hate edm lol)[/b]
bias but i like the genres that comes with SN. The battle music is un-apologetically wub dub cyberpunk-esq synthy EDM music that jumps between dubstep, house, etc. Some of the background environment music then to be tone down in the edm department but still aesthetically fits. What matters IMO is if the music fits the overall SN package and it does

[b]Characters: 7/10[/b]
In the beginning all the characters are some form of anime trope. Even the MCs are basic. Yuito is the basic male shounen MC who is giga dense and super nice while Kasane is the basic female shounen MC who is cold, logical, and blunt. 

Due to the hangout phases, all characters are guaranteed development. Even characters such as Shiden who began insufferable become more understandable and interesting. But of course not all stories are as equal. Stories such Kagero, Arashi, and Gemma are great but the other ones is more subjective.

[b]Gameplay 8/10 [/b]
Gameplay is super fun and engaging. Might as well say it here, this game isn't Code Vain or Genshin impact. Yes its a hack&slash character/team oriented game with dodge mechanics but its unfair to compare to these games. The "closest" would be games from Platinum Game like Nier and Bayo.

While there is not a lot of enemies, the combination of enemies will force you to understand all of your abilities to counter in order to clear the room at a decent rate. Especially late game, if you don't remember how to counter each and good combos (both attack and skill combos) you won't get pass. Its difficult enough for you to focus while the game-play scaling easy enough to pick up. Early on they give you easy enemies but late game, they will literally throw you enemies that was once bosses at you.

The major gripe is the very awkward difficult peaks. While it is easy to pick up, early-mid phases get a bit more difficult b/c you haven't unlocked things such as : combo visions, longer attack combos + extensions, key elements of a character's abilities. Minor spoiler but Kyoka allows you to duplicate items when you throw at enemies but what actually makes her amazing is when you unlock the ability to create duplicates of yourself when attacking, effectively double or tripling you damage output. I don't want to spoil any more but you will find the difficulty to jump up and down throughout the game.

Maps and environments are basic, simple and straightforward. This one is subjective but i find it better to be more dumb b/c it allows more focus on the fighting that progressively gets more complex.

[b] Side content such as character customization, sidequests,etc : 5/10[/b]
This section covers elements outside core gameplay such as side quests, character customization, etc. My god the sidequests are utter trash. A mixture of fetch quests and "kill enemy while doing x". Out of the 50 side-quests, i only did like 5. Its also annoying to find these quests. I just ignore them.

They give you a lot of stuff for Character customization but holy crap, the organization system is so bad. Instead of having 1 item which allows you pick the color you want, they just throw it in the list of stuff you can buy. You will spend a lot of time scrolling through the different color variation of Baki stuff instead of looking at the item you want and picking out the color next. Also there is no preview feature so your buying blind. Luckily the some of the items are cool.

There is no weapon customization at all. The only true difference in weapons for a character is the "+3" attack damage each iteration. Each character gets their own weapon. So for upkeep, you have to buy 9 weapons each time they give you a new version for each character. A lot of lost potential here

The hangout parts are cool thou

[b]Graphics : its stylish/10[/b]
It ain't no crysis but the art style is what drives the graphics. The style hovers around cyber, "brain" punk. The actual world is very boring, drab, and dull but that elevates the aesthetic due the red glowy signs and holograms. This strong contrast allows the already great looking characters and enemies to stand out even more. The character design are are a big mix of tech-wear, cyberpunk, and IT support with all the wires and stuff.

If you can't buy into the aesthetic they are selling, then obviously the graphics would won't be good in your perspective but the "Brainpunk" aesthetic and the original enemy design makes the game look great IMO.

The first time i saw the manga style dialogue presentation, i thought it was meh. They definitely put the animation budget in the gameplay animations (brain crush animations which look amazing). Sad b/c the times they did animate cut-scenes are well animated and directed. The style overtime grew on me though but I can see why someone would hate this.

[b]Overall : 7-8/10[/b]
Fighting fun, characters cool, graphics pretty. A lot of negative elements don't take away from the meat of the what you will be enjoying. Also Arashi is best girl b/c shes represents the collective lazy-ness of weeb and gamers alike.
